properties.evidence: That idea's option (a) is to add `deferred` and `withdrawn` to Decision.status, and its own counter-argument is that a vocabulary change costs every consumer a migration. Measured while writing this node: GraphStamp carries reflow2_version, schema_version, node_types, edge_types, node_type_names and edge_type_names — no enum vocabularies at all. So that change would move NOTHING the version guard reads, and an older binary would open the graph silently and meet a status value it has never heard of. This idea is the mechanism that would make that hazard visible; it answers the hazard that one creates, which is what MITIGATES means here.
